svg.title: TOPAK B9 — A tree of planes: each seated under a charter it can only narrow, bounded as a havoc issuer, fenced by every plane above, and run by replicas whose membership shrinks only by a voted schedule
svg.desc: "No principal grants another, so there is no chain of delegation to attenuate" (ToO §2.11). The custodian asked what follows if TOPAK is the top tier of a command chain, with control planes below it that only narrow ⟨1⟩. ADR-0059 places it: the grantor is a mechanism and not a model, the delegation only attenuates, and it is budgeted. ADR-0061 gives an autonomous plane seven replicas under Byzantine agreement and a membership that shrinks only along a schedule its charter voted, down to a capture floor. Both are Proposed overlays, revised R1 on 2026.11.10 after their modules were checked and proved: R1 narrowed what the budget bounds, and added the one-vote rule. Nothing here is in force and nothing is built.

text.tspan: A tree of planes: each seated under a charter it can only narrow, bounded as a havoc issuer, fenced by every plane above, and run by replicas whose membership shrinks only by a voted schedule

The custodian asked what follows if TOPAK is the top tier of a command chain, with control planes below it that only narrow ⟨1⟩. ADR-0059 places it: the grantor is a mechanism and not a model, the delegation only attenuates, and it is budgeted. ADR-0061 gives an autonomous plane seven replicas under Byzantine agreement and a membership that shrinks only along a

schedule its charter voted, down to a capture floor. Both are Proposed overlays, revised R1 on 2026.11.10 after their modules were checked and proved: R1 narrowed what the budget bounds, and added the one-vote rule. Nothing here is in force and nothing is built.

text.tspan: Proposed · C1 · an overlay, not the archetype
Proposed · C1 · an overlay, not the archetype
Proved · 495 obligations · at five replicas, not seven

svg.text: Proposed means nothing here is in force. C1 applies to ADR-0059 because every grant below the root travels the path it opens, and to ADR-0061 because who may form a certificate is who may grant, and its §3 changes that at run time. C3 applies to neither while each is an overlay ⟨Q11⟩, and would apply on admission to the archetype. What exists is two models: TLC rows are checked at small constants, TLAPS obligations are proved, and each proof module is certified, with 7 (Federation) and 6
(Membership) LS4 temporal steps that no checker confirms. Membership is checked and proved at five replicas, not at §1's seven. One author, one day.

Every field is the parent's or narrower. The comparison is field by field, and it is made three times: ① before the vote, ② when the seating is applied, and ③ by every verifier of the chain (ADR-0033 §4).
A plane is one replica set with one log, one epoch and one set of rules in force. Its parent seats it by voting on a charter, as it votes on any seating (ADR-0024 A3).
A child's budget is debited from its parent's when it is seated. What the debit bounds, and what it does not, is R1's finding (the next band).
ADR-0060, ADR-0061, ADR-0063 and ADR-0064 add fields that only an autonomous plane carries. ADR-0061's is membership (the band on ADR-0061).
§3's table, whole: what kind of act a narrowing is ⟨8⟩ ⟨Q1⟩. "Adding takes a quorum, and denying is local" (ToO §7.10)

A promotion. "Everything crossing from Build to Run is promoted" (ToO §7.1)

A narrowing is a promotion when it brings a new issuer or a new artifact into force. Otherwise it is an admit, ordered by the plane's consensus and signed by one person or by the mechanism ⟨Q1⟩. "Quorum" in the last three rows means the replicas' agreement
on the order, and no vote.

text.tspan: §2 · Policy narrows by composition, and there is one floor ⟨Q8⟩
At any admit or permit, at any plane, the decision is the floor's permit and no refusal from any bundle on the chain.

svg.text: A bundle a lower plane adds is appended, can refuse, and is never asked whether to grant (ToO §3.1).
So "narrower than the parent" holds of the composed decision for every bundle, at every plane, at every age. This is ADR-0030's argument applied once per link, and nothing compares two policies.
One floor serves the whole tree ⟨Q8⟩. Every charter carries the root's floor digest. Planes differ by bundles only.

text.tspan: §4 · A plane is a havoc issuer, bounded by its charter

svg.text: ADR-0025 treats the anchor as a havoc issuer bounded by the rules floor. A plane gets the same treatment, bounded by its charter.

text.tspan: Whatever a plane signs, a verifier accepts only what every charter on the chain allows.

svg.text: A captured plane therefore chooses among leases its parent's quorum already voted acceptable: it decides which, never whether.
⟨R1⟩ The chain check bounds what each lease may carry, and not how many a captured plane signs (§1).

text.tspan: §5 · Why crash-recovery cannot supply a certificate ⟨Q7⟩

svg.text: Every charter and every lease carries a commit certificate: signatures from a quorum of the issuing plane's replicas over the entry's digest and log index.
A crash-recovery protocol cannot supply that certificate: one lying replica can obtain a majority's signatures for two entries at one index, in two ballots.
A plane whose replicas can be captured declares it, and runs Byzantine agreement ⟨Q7⟩. An autonomous plane is always such a plane (ADR-0061).
A plane that declares its replicas unexposed keeps the corpus's consensus, and its certificates are trusted on that declaration.

What survives capture is the honest parent's account and each honest governor's bound (ADR-0063 §3). Nothing in the chain check can refuse the third lease.

text.tspan: As drafted: "the root's tally bounds the whole tree"

svg.text: It fails under capture (History, R1; Federation.tla's header). The debit bounds what is allocated.
A captured plane can sign more leases than its budget, each to a different vehicle, and no single verifier sees more than its own, so nothing in the model
can refuse them.

text.tspan: §4 and the Consequences say the same ⟨R1⟩

svg.text: §4: the chain check bounds what each lease may carry, and not how many a captured plane signs.
Positive: what a captured plane's lease may carry is bounded by its charter, and the bound is checked by whoever receives the lease. How many it
Leases issued under a charter and under every charter below it never exceed its budget, for a subtree with no captured plane. That it is stated so is
a finding (the module's header).
Checked in every budget row with Captured={}, and broken by M_NODEBIT alone. Proved as BudgetConservedAlways, resting on Account.

text.tspan: Any plane fences everything below it, the trusted base, and the overlay (ADR-0059 §6–§8)
§6 · Any plane on the chain fences everything below it ⟨9⟩

svg.text: A charter and a lease carry the epoch and log index of each plane on the chain, not only the granting plane's. An admit or a permit compares each against the
latest its verifier has heard.
A plane that moves its epoch fences everything below it. That act is a plane fence: a subtraction, ordered, needing no quorum (ToO §4.1).
A fence travels as far as the link does. What bounds a plane the fence cannot reach is ADR-0063.

text.tspan: Each plane's replicas are a row of the kind T-0045-1, per plane.

svg.text: Where §5 applies, Byzantine agreement replaces that row, and a forged certificate is its failure. ADR-0068 carries the rows.
Negative: a deeper trusted base, a replica row per plane, and a chain every verifier must walk.

text.tspan: §8 · An overlay, and what is reported upstream ⟨Q11⟩

svg.text: ADR-0023 §4: a variation that holds a capability the archetype lacks is not a rung. So this is an overlay's record, and reports under ADR-0058 §6: a mechanism
that grants below itself, bounded by a charter; commit certificates a third party can check with no plane in reach; a fence that names every plane on a chain.
If the archetype takes them, its records owe: ADR-0054's sentence on delegation and ToO §2.11, restated; ADR-0024 A3; ADR-0031, the lease's fence one per
plane; ADR-0045's decision not to require Byzantine agreement, reversed for exposed planes, which is C3. A one-plane deployment would then be a declared
degeneracy.

Negative (Consequences): delegation. It attenuates, it is a mechanism's and it is budgeted, and it is still delegation. Byzantine agreement is required wherever replicas are exposed, which the corpus had declined to require.

text.tspan: An autonomous plane: seven replicas, and a membership that shrinks only along a voted schedule (ADR-0061)

svg.text: §1's table, whole: seven replicas, tolerating two captured ⟨20⟩

text.tspan: Captured or slow tolerated, for the duration bound (ADR-0064)

svg.text: A certificate for n replicas tolerating f captured is the least whole number above (n + f) / 2, so that any two certificates share an honest signer. Why seven and not four: four replicas tolerate one capture or one loss, and have no smaller membership to fall

back to that tolerates any capture. Seven tolerate two of either at once, and have three steps of the schedule above a floor of one. The number is a placeholder, as every number in the corpus is until something is measured.

text.tspan: §2 · The instrument is PBFT at the reference, on two conditions ⟨20⟩

svg.text: The letters name roles, not products (ToO §1). What the pattern asks of P at an exposed plane is Byzantine agreement whose certificates a third party can check (ADR-0059 §5). PBFT (Castro and Liskov, 1999) gives agreement at n = 3f + 1
with certificates of 2f + 1 (recalled, not re-read).

1. Its messages must be signed. A governor verifies a certificate with no plane in reach. A later form of PBFT replaced signatures with message authentication codes, which convince only the replica they were made for (recalled). That form
cannot supply a commit certificate.
2. It needs a reconfiguration step. PBFT as published has a fixed membership (recalled). §3 adds a step that changes it, and that step is where an error would be an error about authority.

Three things fit as they are: ADR-0064's rules are conditions on a replica's vote; the view change runs on timeouts, which is liveness; a Byzantine primary chooses the order and can stall, and cannot forge, so it decides which and never
whether.
§3: the membership shrinks along a schedule voted in the charter ⟨19⟩, here §4's archetype: 7, 6, 5, 4, with a capture floor of one ⟨Q18⟩

A step drops one replica. Any replica may propose to drop one it has not heard for a declared number of ticks (ADR-0064). A replica signs the proposal only if it has
not heard that replica either.
The membership being replaced orders the step, by its own certificate. So a membership has at most one successor, and a minority cut off by a partition
A dropped replica does not return below the intent boundary. Adding a replica brings an issuer into force, which is a promotion (ADR-0059 §3). Its vehicle may
still hold a lease if it hears the plane again (drafter's choice).
No step takes the plane below the floor, and no other change of membership is allowed (FD13, FD4).

text.tspan: ⟨R1⟩ One vote per membership, and the split vote that stalls

svg.text: An honest replica signs at most one step of a membership. The first rule does not give this: a replica that has heard neither of two others could sign both drops,
and two successors follow (M_TWOVOTES).
§2's agreement gives it: one entry at one log index, with a step that names the membership it replaces.
Read as one vote per membership with no second ballot, a vote that splits stalls the schedule for good: safe, and not live. The plane keeps its size, and a
further loss may end it (Negative).
Open: whether a split vote may be retried. Membership.tla has no ballot and no view change, so a retry that keeps AtMostOneSuccessor is neither designed nor
checked.

text.tspan: Negative: it strains a mechanism constant, "a timeout is never a grant" (ADR-0024)

svg.text: A step adds nothing to the charter: no entry, no budget, no longer life. But silence is what triggers it, and what it preserves is a plane's ability to grant.
The record accepts that because the schedule and the floor were voted, because the step is ordered by a quorum and not taken by default, and because the
alternative is that one loss beyond what the plane tolerates leaves no certificate ever again (Context; the NATO reading's N3).
If the archetype takes it, ADR-0024 owes a statement of how §3 stands beside the constant, and ADR-0045 the replica row with the reconfiguration step, which
§4's table, whole ⟨Q18⟩

text.tspan: Losses survived, one at a time
At this schedule the floor adds nothing ⟨R1⟩

svg.text: The schedule is 7, 6, 5, 4 and the capture floor is one. Four is the last
size that tolerates one capture, so the floor adds nothing the schedule
does not.
The floor binds a charter whose schedule runs past it. In the model,
m-below-archetype holds.

text.tspan: A smaller membership may carry a smaller budget ⟨Q17⟩

svg.text: A charter may give each membership its own budget. Where the tally
states one, a step narrows what the plane holds as well as lowering what
it takes to capture it. Where it states none, the budget is unchanged.
The quorum dial of the lattice analysis: capture is how many captured
holders it takes to grant; loss is how many silent holders still let a grant
happen.
At an autonomous plane the replicas are exposed and nobody else
grants, so the pair applies to them. A step spends the first to restore

text.tspan: It keeps agreement and tolerates one capture. It has no schedule,
and one loss beyond the first ends it.

svg.text: Other Negatives. Against an adversary that can silence vehicles, the tolerance is the floor's from the start: jamming honest vehicles until their replicas are dropped walks the plane down its schedule, and two captured replicas then capture a plane that tolerated two when it was seated. A reconfiguration step no published PBFT has, in the trusted base. Cost unmeasured: PBFT's messages grow with the square of the membership. One author, one day, and an instrument described from memory. Positive: a plane
outlives its first losses, four one at a time where a fixed seven survives two, and a partition still leaves at most one plane.

text.tspan: Two mutations break two properties each

svg.text: M_LASTLINK and M_TRUSTPLANE each break LeaseWithinChain and HavocPlaneBounded: under capture, a lease outside the chain is, or can be, outside what the root voted. Proposal §10 asked for one property each. With no plane captured, both
hold LeaseWithinChain (m-last-honest, m-trust-honest).

A chain of three planes, r → a → b, with r the root. A sibling would only be a second debit against the same left.
Four of §1's fields: seated, alphabet, budget and fence. labels, bundles, ttlMax, countMax and expiry have the shape of the first two.
A commit certificate is taken as unforgeable. A presented lease is any entry and epoch, under any plane, so a property that holds rests on the verifier's checks alone. Verifiers are honest.
The root's tally is honest. A plane is not re-seated. Membership is Membership.tla's. Deadlock is not checked: a chain that is seated and spent is safe.

text.tspan: Two findings, both taken into the record by R1

svg.text: The one-vote rule was not in §3. M_TWOVOTES shows two successors follow without it. The module takes it as the honest replica's rule; §3 now says so.
At the archetype the floor is redundant with the schedule: m-below-archetype holds. M_BELOWFLOOR's breaking rows run with a schedule that passes the floor. §4 now says so.
Four witnesses, each violated, so each constrained behaviour is reachable
a step is ordered
the plane reaches four replicas
honest votes of one membership split between two drops
a certificate that orders a step includes a captured replica
Five replicas, one plane. §1's seven is not modelled.
PBFT is abstracted to its certificate: no primary, no view change, no message delivery, no ballot. §7's "PBFT is read" is not met by this module, nor the measurement.
"Not heard" is not modelled: an honest replica may sign any drop but its own, which is more than §3 allows. A step's ticks (ADR-0064) and a smaller membership's budget (§4) are not modelled.
A step only removes: no action adds a replica, since that is a promotion. Deadlock is not checked: a plane at its floor with every vote cast is safe.

Open obligations. ADR-0059: the floor stage and the reference; the custodian's reading of every drafter's choice; the findings of the two readings this set does not answer (F3, F4, N1, N2, Z2, Z3 and the rest of Z4; F4 bears on §1: the charter has no field for an envelope in the world); ToO and the glossary owe "plane", "charter", "chain", "commit certificate" and "plane fence" if the archetype takes this. ADR-0061: the reading of PBFT, the measurement and the reference; whether a split vote may be retried; where an

autonomous plane's orchestrator runs (if on one vehicle, its loss stalls every decision point: N3); the number of silent ticks before a replica may be dropped; whether a dropped replica's vehicle may hold a lease.
